questions.q: What is Azure Data Factory, in one sentence?
options: A programming language for writing ETL scripts
A managed cloud service for orchestrating and automating data movement and transformation at scale
A relational database engine for storing transactional data
A visualization tool for building dashboards
questions.explain: Data Factory doesn't store your data or visualize it — it moves and transforms data between other systems, on a managed, automated, monitorable platform.

questions.q: Which Data Factory component defines the connection information needed to reach a data store or compute resource?
questions.explain: A linked service works like a connection string. A dataset then points to the specific structure of data inside whatever the linked service connects to.

options: A scheduled time for a data factory to run
A logical grouping of activities that together perform one unit of work
The compute environment an activity runs on
questions.explain: Activities are the individual steps (like copying data); a pipeline groups them so they can be managed, run, and monitored as one unit rather than individually.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four workflow stages Data Factory is built around?
questions.explain: The four stages are connect & collect, transform & enrich, CI/CD & publish, and monitor. Visualizing the results is a job for a tool like Power BI, downstream of Data Factory.

questions.q: What kind of data scenario is Data Factory specifically built to handle well?
options: Only data already inside Azure SQL Database
Hybrid scenarios — data spread across both on-premises and cloud sources
questions.explain: Data Factory's integration runtime concept exists specifically to bridge on-premises and cloud sources securely — a scenario that's expensive to build custom tooling for.
